issues.legal_issue: A retired public servant may use a special summary procedure to recover rented premises only if the landlord-tenant relationship existed when the public servant retired.
material_facts: The landlord retired from public service before the tenant was inducted into the premises.
The landlord later sought possession for his own residence using a special summary eviction procedure.
The Rent Controller and High Court allowed the eviction application, but the Supreme Court set aside their orders.
issues.conclusion: Because the landlord was not the landlord of the premises qua the tenant at the time of retirement, he was not entitled to maintain the summary eviction application; the appeal was allowed and the orders below were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 2(hh) and 13-A of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction (Amendment) Act, 1985, the applicant must have been entitled to receive rent for the premises from the tenant when the applicant retired from public service. The later filing window in Section 13-A does not remove this requirement. The Court approved Sohan Singh v. Dhan Raj Sharma and Bhanu Aththayya v. Comdr. Kaushal, and applied the principle in Mrs. Winifred Ross v. Mrs. Ivy Fonseca that the landlord must have been landlord qua both the premises and the tenant at retirement.

predicates.special_summary_eviction_application: A landlord filed an application using a special summary procedure to recover rented premises from a tenant.
predicates.retired_from_public_service: The landlord had retired from public service.
predicates.landlord_tenant_relationship_at_retireme: The landlord was entitled to receive rent from that tenant for those premises when the landlord retired.
predicates.special_summary_eviction_application_not: The landlord's application using the special summary eviction procedure cannot be maintained.

issues.definition: When a retired public servant uses a special summary eviction procedure but was not the tenant's landlord for the premises at retirement, the application cannot be maintained.
